officialReport.caveat: Conversion summaries remain scoped to the last single-rule conversion; solution-wide pending-review counts below come from the current detection YAML.

detectionDependencyPlan.bindings: Each record retains its exact original and converted query hashes, table proposals and uncertainty.

workbookDependencyPlan.bindings: Each of 290 records retains workbook identity/hash, query pointer/hash and raw proposal. Scanner false positives are not accepted prerequisites.

remainingTiming.caveat: Regex lineage and an accepted service-window difference do not prove table binding, event-time equivalence, aggregation parity or runtime correctness.

hostMappings.caveat: Custom details do not restore entity identity or correlation; runtime output binding and size limits remain unverified.

additionalFindings: LocalAdminGroupChanges and PotentialCobaltStrikeRansomwareActivity carry time-column/mixed-workload warnings even though static dependency proposals identify native tables.
SUNSPOTHashes has an isfuzzy-union binding finding.

technicalFailures: ImminentRansomware depends on _ASim_ProcessEvent; workspace functions cannot simply be installed for Custom Detections.
PossiblePhishingwithCSL&NetworkSession also uses _Im_NetworkSession, which the conservative dependency plan does not fully represent.
The source Phishing rule's AWSS3 declaration uses datatypes instead of dataTypes for AWSVPCFlow. The generated connector metadata is structurally invalid; accepting a review cannot remove this error.
PossibleWebpBufferOverflow has an unresolved output-binding finding for DeviceName; retaining a provisional mapping is not a resolution.

workbooks.caveat: These four tables are documented native Defender for Office 365 inputs, not missing workspace functions. Current scanner/planner classifications still require supported resolution; documentation does not prove tenant availability or runtime compatibility.

descriptionReplacements.5bdc1504-880c-4b30-a39c-7c746535928d: Detects PsExec-origin PowerShell commands that stop services and contain both SQL and Exchange tokens. This activity can precede human-operated ransomware execution.
descriptionReplacements.47c02e21-3949-4e05-a28e-576cd75ff6f6: Detects cmd-launched ping activity with calc.exe, loopback and delay tokens associated with Qakbot self-deletion.
descriptionReplacements.174de33b-107b-4cd8-a85d-b4025a35453f: Detects Word, Excel or Outlook launching wscript.exe to execute a JScript Encoded file. This behavior is associated with malicious Office macros and Trickbot activity.
descriptionReplacements.35ab0d58-baab-4154-87ed-fa2f69797e9e: Detects PsExec-like command activity creating more than four distinct remote executable paths in ten-minute bins, after configured exclusions. This behavior can indicate ransomware propagation.
